It was a happy thought on the part of those as- anointed with Wycliffe Congregational Church to celebrate the completion of the Rev. John Tongs'. 21 years' of ministerial service in Warrington by a congregational gathering. In both towns last Saturday a very large amount of interest wan centred in the fixture between Ruin- corn and Warrington. For years the match has been contested with equal determination on both aid is, but 80 far Runcorn have hail much the best of it. This season the two clubs ha.e shown very good form, and while Warrington have Ibsen de. Gutted by narrow majorities on two or three oche. sions, the t7hoshire organisation has only had to bow the knee once. The teams are still wholly com- posed of local players, so that the battle is a fair one in every respect. A special train conveyed the ! Warrington team and about I,soClsupporters to Run. corn.while many more went by 'bus,bike or on foot, to that the I rwell-lane enclosure contained a goodly sprinkling of Warringtonians. The home crowd wa. there in unusually strong force, and a gate" of about 6,000 contributed substantially to the Club's exchequer. Jolley was the only absentee on the Runcorn side while the Warrington team turned out as relnAed. Mr. Priestley of Broughton Rangers was the referee. The players were as follows : .

Another infringement of the rules by the hoomesters relieved Warrington. but from Taylor's mark, Houghton had a try at goal,the ball going far wide.. Some useful kicking was in- dulged in by both antes, and though the honeetere still remained in the Warrington half they could melee no head way. Faulkner put ins short kick from the peek which Bosco., sectored, hut wan tackled. The Visitors' position was now a precerioue ormand Houghton punting to the centre Irons touch almost, led tea score. With tile game waging hotly un- der the poste, Bate trickily got away and kicked out,Barber racing finely to the centre and securing the ball just as Houghton cense up end rolled him in touch. Duckworth meetly added to the advan- tage, and the forwards dribbled into the Runcorn half. Then Faulkner got away only to lot laid low by Naylor. Runcorn returned to the attack and Butterworth made a feeble drop at goal, Boscow touching down. Smart following up by the viii- core called upon Houghton who was polled down by Duckworth. Bate, Duckworth, and Isherwood exchanged well, nail then Rotoineon, Faulkner, and Williamson followed suit, the latter knocking on. Another effort was made by Duckworth. Bate, and Barber, the latter running well until William- eon moot him in touch. Again Barber got brilliantly away, and looked liked scoring, when the touch. flag went up amid groane from the sinking opects• tore. After thiebrief isseault on the home citadel Warrington had to retire, and Duckworth in at- tempting to kick out, had the bellcharged down by Butterworth, who scored a soft try. Houghton easily added a goal. Thus unexpectedly the homes. tern were presented with five points, and for a few moments looked like running over their oppon- rate. W•rrington rallied well however, and Moores hurt hinvielf in tackling the burly Runcorn custodian. Dakin and Fairhurst placed Warrington on the offensive, end from the next scrimmage Duckworth gat clear, but Butterworth was on eim before he passed. div.p: IMPENDING DEPARTURE OF REV. DR. PRESTON FROM RUNCORN.

On Sunday evening,. the close of his sermon, at the Trinity Churcln,Runcurn, the pastor, the Rev. Dr. Free- ton.mado an announcement which had a startling effect upon those present. He said—Before closing I have an anamincement to make which will doubtless be • aur- trine to you. I take the very earliest opportunity of r forming you about a matter of much importance to this pari, h It is one also in which you all are very directly intereated,from the youngest to the oldest. It has to to with the welfare and prooperity of this church,and with all belonging to H. My pnaiti n and my feelings are much thom of the Apostle Paul when at Miletus. He addressed the Presbyter, of the Church of Ephosua in wordn a follows And now tvhold I know that ye among whom I have gone preaching the kingdom of Ood shall nee my face no more.'' I am constrained to use similar language. My ministry amongst you ia all hut ended. In • few lIPPks at most it will all he over. The Lord Bishop of Cheater, with the kindhearted• nese and conai&ranion which do characterise hint, has most kindly offered me another living. The offer has come unsought and unsolicited, and 111,11 t on. expectedly. Thin adds to its value, as well as ciAning (rim iltrcateenteif and fair-dealing Bishop, arty, has treated me with much kindness ever slow he came tat the dineme.
